issues.legal_issue: A suit for ejectment following the expiry of a fixed-term lease is maintainable without a notice to quit when the tenancy has not continued by holding over.
material_facts: A registered lease granted possession for a fixed term, with options for two further fixed terms; the lease term commenced when the tenant obtained the required licence.
The lease term expired by efflux of time before the ejectment suit was filed.
The tenant did not claim to be holding over, and there was no allegation that the landlord had assented to continued possession after the lease expired.
issues.conclusion: The lease expired by efflux of time, so a notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 was not necessary and the ejectment suit was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 111(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a lease for a definite term is determined by efflux of time. Section 106 notice is not required when the lease ends in that way. Sections 111(a) and 116 must be read together: continuation by holding over requires possession after determination of the lease and the lessor's express or implied assent. Pleadings cannot alter the intrinsic character of the lease or the rights and obligations arising from it. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: ejectment_suit_based_on_fixed_term_expiry and fixed_term_lease_expired_by_time and not lessor_assented_to_post_expiry_possession

predicates.ejectment_suit_based_on_fixed_term_expir: The proceeding is an ejectment suit based on the expiry of a fixed-term lease.
predicates.fixed_term_lease_expired_by_time: The lease was for a definite term and that term ended by efflux of time.
predicates.lessor_assented_to_post_expiry_possessio: The lessor expressly or impliedly assented to the tenant's possession after the lease ended.

issues.definition: When an ejectment suit rests on the expiry of a definite lease term and the lessor did not assent to possession continuing after expiry, the suit does not require a notice to quit.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant whose contractual tenancy has ended is not a statutory tenant under a tenancy statute that applies to municipalities but not to notified areas outside municipalities.
material_facts: The premises were in an area constituted as a notified area, rather than a municipality.
The statutory-tenancy point had been decided against the tenant at trial and was not pressed before the appellate courts.
issues.conclusion: The tenant did not become a statutory tenant because the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956 applied to municipalities and not to the notified area where the premises were situated.
issues.legal_principle: The West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956 extended to municipalities and did not apply to a notified area merely because it had been constituted as one. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.statutory_tenancy_claim_after_contract_e: The claim is that an occupant became a statutory tenant after the contractual tenancy ended.
predicates.premises_in_notified_area: The premises are situated in an area constituted as a notified area.
predicates.premises_outside_municipality: The premises are outside a municipality.
predicates.tenancy_protection_limited_to_municipali: The relevant tenancy protection applies to municipalities and not to notified areas outside municipalities.

issues.definition: When the contractual tenancy has ended, the premises are in a notified area outside a municipality, and the tenancy protection is limited to municipalities, the occupant does not become a statutory tenant under that protection.
